content: The private sector must assume responsibility for the proper management of healthcare waste generated by the products and services they provide. This includes designing products and packaging that minimize waste and facilitate safe disposal. The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued recommendations for healthcare waste management systems. These guidelines emphasize the importance of sound waste management practices to protect public health and the environment. In response to the global educational initiative The World’s Largest Lesson, UNICEF Romania launched a project to promote the responsible disposal of used face masks and other personal protective equipment (PPE) during the COVID-19 pandemic. Teachers and students collaborated to educate communities on the proper disposal of items such as masks, gloves, and antibacterial wipes. The initiative aimed to reduce the risks of viral contamination and environmental pollution by encouraging the use of closed containers for waste collection. Tens of thousands of Romanian children have been educated on these practices, and they are now actively raising awareness about the environmental impact of improperly discarded PPE. The COVID-19 pandemic has led to a significant increase in the use of self-care products, such as face masks, hand sanitizers, and plastic gloves, resulting in a global rise in medical waste. For example, during the peak of the outbreak in Wuhan, China, hospitals generated over six times their usual amount of waste, most of which consisted of plastic PPE. The safe disposal of this waste is critical not only for reducing viral transmission but also for mitigating its environmental impact, such as the release of microplastic fibers from face masks. These challenges highlight the need for further research and policy changes to address solid waste management during and after the pandemic. The WHO has also emphasized the importance of self-care interventions for health and well-being. These interventions include strategies to support individuals in managing their health, such as the use of digital tools, mobile health applications, and community-based programs. The organization has provided guidelines to optimize healthcare systems and improve access to essential services, particularly in low-resource settings. The pandemic has underscored the need for innovative approaches to healthcare delivery, including task shifting and the integration of community health workers into primary care systems. These measures aim to enhance access to healthcare services while maintaining quality and efficiency. In addition, the WHO has highlighted the importance of addressing the social determinants of health and promoting equity in healthcare access. This includes ensuring that vulnerable populations, such as women, children, and older adults, receive the care they need throughout their life course. The global health community must continue to prioritize sustainable development goals, including universal health coverage, environmental protection, and the promotion of health equity. Collaborative efforts between governments, organizations, and communities are essential to achieving these objectives and improving health outcomes worldwide.
